sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why is 'manipulation' considered unethical in photojournalism?
questions.answer: Because the photojournalist must capture the truth; manipulating or staging an image is like making up a news story.

questions.q: Discuss any two qualities of a photojournalist.
questions.answer: Alertness and readiness to act fast with the camera at hand; patience and winning the trust of people; truthfulness.

questions.q: Name any two famous photojournalists of India with their work.
questions.answer: Raghu Rai – photographs of Indira Gandhi and Bhopal gas tragedy; Homai Vyarawalla – first woman photojournalist covering World War II.

questions.q: What is meant by ethics in photojournalism?
questions.answer: The moral principles that guide a photojournalist, truthfulness being the core.

questions.q: What is the role of a photo editor in choosing pictures?
questions.answer: He chooses what appears by considering the major news of the day, the hard-hitting nature of the photo and reader interest.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss the importance of ethics in photojournalism.
questions.answer: Truthfulness is a core ethic; in the digital age manipulation is easy but violates ethics; photographers must not stage or invent situations, so the picture remains a truthful record that readers trust.

questions.q: What is meant by ethics? What can be counted as the core ethics for a photojournalist?
questions.answer: Ethics are moral principles governing journalism; for a photojournalist the core ethic is truthfulness: no manipulation, no staging, photograph only what happened when it happened.

questions.q: Explain the role played by famous photojournalists in India before and after Independence.
questions.answer: Raja Deen Dayal, Sunil Janah and Homai Vyarawalla recorded British India, partition and the freedom movement; Henri Cartier-Bresson, Raghu Rai and Prashant Panjiar documented events and leaders after independence.
